mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 1% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the month following the rate hike (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength boosts corporate optimism and investment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 60-day return during prior months with lower PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of 10% or more predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weakening housing demand and reduced corporate earnings momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥10% over two consecutive months prior to prediction
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of similar contraction events (back-tested).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (industrial production) of 3% or more for three consecutive months indicates supply-side expansion, which is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return via stronger earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥3% monthly for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO momentum and SPX 60-day forward returns in analogous past recovery periods (Pearson ρ < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for the first time in three months, it triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as low unemployment supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in the current month after ≥3 months at or above 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in 3 out of 5 historical episodes of similar unemployment declines (back-tested).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of 2% or more suggest dual demand weakness, which predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return due to near-term profit compression.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% AND RSAFS decreases by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in analogous historical dual-demand shocks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a regime where PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000 jobs for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals labor market resilience and corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 20-day forward return in 5 prior analogous labor expansions (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL (CPI) prints a monthly increase above 0.3% for the first time in a month of steady inflation, it predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return as markets anticipate future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% in a month with ≤0.2% prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in 4 historical episodes of similar CPI spikes (back-tested).
